home.feature1Desc: Create multiple Minecraft instances with different versions, mods and settings, all organized in one place.
home.feature2Desc: The code is open on GitHub. Audit it, tweak it or contribute.
home.feature3Desc: Supports Premium, NoPremium and Ely.by accounts. Switch between profiles securely and without friction.
home.feature4Desc: It uses few resources and keeps a stable performance, even on lower-end hardware.
home.feature5Desc: Tune the launcher behavior and Minecraft settings to match your preferences.
home.feature6Desc: Install mods, modloaders, texture packs and check logs directly from the launcher.
home.feature7Desc: CubicLauncher is not a fork. It was built from scratch, with every component designed for the project.
home.feature8Desc: Completely change the launcher's appearance with community and verified themes, or create your own.
home.feature9Desc: Import your existing instances from the official launcher or others like MultiMC and its forks, without having to set everything up again from scratch.
home.mission: Our goal is for anyone to play Minecraft with a stable, fast launcher under their own control. CubicLauncher is free, open source and compatible with Premium, NoPremium and Ely.by accounts.
home.valueSubtitle: A launcher built to deliver real performance, freedom and accessibility. No forced premium accounts, no ads, and the user stays in control.
home.value1Desc: No hidden costs, subscriptions or restrictions. Download it, use it and adapt it to your needs.
home.value2Desc: Uses few resources and keeps a stable execution across different systems.
home.value3Desc: Available for Windows, Linux and macOS. The same experience on any of the three.
home.value4Desc: Personalize the launcher's appearance with community themes and tailor it to the way you play.
home.value5Desc: We didn't inherit code from other launchers. Every line was written in this repository.
home.quickStartSubtitle: Select your operating system, download the installer and open CubicLauncher.

about.title: About
about.paragraph1: CubicLauncher was born in Rust, built by a Spanish-speaking team. We designed it as a launcher with a clean, modern interface that never feels intrusive, without sacrificing performance or features.
about.paragraph2: We also want you to customize it with community-made themes and keep control over your experience.
about.paragraph3: Being open source under the GPL license, anyone can review how it works. That brings more trust and transparency.
about.paragraph4: We didn't start from a fork. CubicLauncher is developed from scratch, with custom crates tailored to what we need.
about.contributeDescription: You can report bugs, suggest ideas, create themes or submit code on GitHub. Every contribution helps.

virusTotalWarning.bannerTitle: Does VirusTotal or another antivirus flag CubicLauncher?
virusTotalWarning.bannerText: VirusTotal can produce false positives with CubicLauncher. Not everything VirusTotal or another virus scanner reports confirms that the file is malicious.
virusTotalWarning.bannerSource: That is what the source code is for: the launcher is compiled from that code, which is published on GitHub for anyone to review.
virusTotalWarning.reviewCode: View the source code on GitHub
virusTotalWarning.readGuide: What does it mean, and what should I do?
virusTotalWarning.pageTitle: VirusTotal and other antivirus warnings when installing CubicLauncher
virusTotalWarning.pageDescription: What a VirusTotal or other antivirus warning on CubicLauncher means and why it is usually a false positive.
virusTotalWarning.intro: VirusTotal and other scanners may flag CubicLauncher as malicious. Here is what Tauri’s official reports say about this issue and how to check it yourself.
virusTotalWarning.whatText: VirusTotal collects the results of dozens of antivirus engines in a single report. When one or two engines flag a file and the rest do not, the signal is weak: scanners work with patterns and heuristics, not proof. An isolated warning does not confirm that a file is malicious, which is why the full report matters more than the alert count.
virusTotalWarning.whyTitle: Why CubicLauncher shows up in scanners
virusTotalWarning.whyText: CubicLauncher is built with Tauri v2 (Rust and SvelteKit) and on Windows it is distributed as an NSIS installer: the combination scanners flag most often. This is a known issue in the Tauri project, reported in its official repository by developers of other applications whose recent builds are flagged as trojans.
virusTotalWarning.sourcesText: Official documentation and public reports from the Tauri project about false positives and antivirus warnings:
virusTotalWarning.src4749Text: A closed report where a developer uploads their installer to VirusTotal and gets Trojan.Heur detections on the .msi, the main .exe and sidecars, even when building in an isolated environment.
virusTotalWarning.src2486Text: An open report labeled type: bug and platform: Windows about Windows Defender and other antivirus alerts on Tauri applications.
virusTotalWarning.src10649Text: A closed report from a developer whose Tauri 2 packages were consistently flagged by Windows Defender without containing malware.
virusTotalWarning.srcDocsText: The official documentation explains that code signing and reputation are built over time: a warning does not prove the application is malicious.
virusTotalWarning.stepOne: Compare the SHA256 of the file you downloaded with the one published on this page and on GitHub Releases.
virusTotalWarning.stepTwo: Look at the whole report: one or two antivirus hits among dozens are usually false positives.
virusTotalWarning.stepThree: Review the source code: the launcher is compiled from that code on GitHub, and anyone can reproduce the build.
virusTotalWarning.openSourceText: The code CubicLauncher was compiled from is on GitHub. Anyone can view it, review it and build it again.

windowsWarning.bannerTitle: Does Windows show a warning when you open CubicLauncher?
windowsWarning.bannerText: Windows cannot confirm who published the installer because we do not have a digital signature identifying it.
windowsWarning.bannerCost: That signature costs over $300 USD per year. The code is on GitHub, where anyone can review it.
windowsWarning.readGuide: What does it mean, and what should I do?
windowsWarning.pageDescription: What a Windows warning means when installing CubicLauncher and how to check that you downloaded the official installer.
windowsWarning.intro: When you open CubicLauncher, Windows may show “Unknown publisher” or a SmartScreen warning. Here’s what those messages mean and how to check that you downloaded the official installer.
windowsWarning.publisherText: The installer does not have a digital label (called a “signature”) that tells Windows who published it. That is why Windows says “Unknown publisher.” The warning does not tell you whether the file is safe or dangerous; it only means Windows could not confirm who published it.
windowsWarning.smartScreenText: SmartScreen is a warning Windows may show when a downloaded app is new or not yet well known. It may appear together with “Unknown publisher.” The warning alone does not tell you whether the file is safe or dangerous.
windowsWarning.certificateText: Windows needs a digital signature to show who published an installer. It costs over $300 USD per year, and as a community project, we cannot afford it right now.
windowsWarning.stepOne: Download it from this official website or from GitHub, where we publish CubicLauncher.
windowsWarning.stepTwo: If a warning appears, make sure you downloaded the file from one of those sources. If you are not sure where it came from, cancel and download it again from here.
windowsWarning.stepThree: If you want to open it, click “More info” and then “Run anyway.” If you are unsure, close the window and do not open it.
windowsWarning.openSourceText: The code used to build CubicLauncher is published on GitHub. Anyone can view and review it.

platforms.windowsReq: Windows 10 64-bit or later. 4GB RAM minimum recommended.
platforms.windowsStep2: Run the file. If Windows SmartScreen shows a warning, click 'More info' and then 'Run anyway'.
platforms.windowsStep4: Launch CubicLauncher from the Start menu.
platforms.linuxDesc: Universal AppImage for most Linux distributions.
platforms.linuxStep2: Right-click the downloaded file, select 'Properties', go to the 'Permissions' tab, and check 'Allow executing file as program'. Alternatively, run chmod +x cubiclauncher.AppImage in the terminal.
platforms.macosDesc: Universal application for Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3) and Intel processors.
platforms.macosStep2: Open the file and drag the CubicLauncher icon to the Applications folder.
platforms.macosStep3: The first time you open it, macOS may prevent it from running. Go to System Settings > Privacy & Security and click 'Open Anyway'.
